competences: The learner find missing dimensions using area.
The learner calculate perimeter from known area and width.
languageCompetence: Reads, pronounces, spells and correctly uses: rectangle, length, width, area, perimeter.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to find missing dimensions using area.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to calculate perimeter from known area and width.
priorKnowledge: Learners know the formulae for rectangle area and perimeter.
materials: Rectangle cards labelled with area and one side
Chart showing area and perimeter formulae
references: P 6 Primary SIX MTC Notes Docx (ecolebooks Com)

steps.content: Learners know the formulae for rectangle area and perimeter. Starter: A rectangle has area 45 square decimetres and width 5 dm. Find its perimeter.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays rectangle cards labelled with area and one side, reviews the prior skill, and asks: "A rectangle has area 45 square decimetres and width 5 dm. Find its perimeter." The teacher records learners’ methods and connects them to area and perimeter of a rectangle.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous skill, read the starter question, and explain which measurements or operations they would use.

steps.stage: Development: Area and perimeter of rectangles
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: $\text{Area}=\text{length}\times\text{width}$. $\text{Width}=\text{area}\div\text{length}$. $\text{Length}=\text{area}\div\text{width}$. $\text{Perimeter}=2(\text{length}+\text{width})$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: width from area: The area of a rectangle is $56\text{ cm}^2$ and its length is $8\text{ cm}$. Find its width. $\text{Length}\times\text{width}=\text{area}$. $8w=56$. $w=56\div8=7\text{ cm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: The area of a rectangle is $56\text{ cm}^2$ and its length is $8\text{ cm}$. Find its width. $\text{Length}\times\text{width}=\text{area}$. $8w=56$. $w=56\div8=7\text{ cm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: length from area: A rectangular piece of paper has area $4800\text{ mm}^2$ and width $60\text{ mm}$. Find its length. $\text{Length}\times\text{width}=\text{area}$. $60L=4800$. $L=4800\div60=80\text{ mm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: A rectangular piece of paper has area $4800\text{ mm}^2$ and width $60\text{ mm}$. Find its length. $\text{Length}\times\text{width}=\text{area}$. $60L=4800$. $L=4800\div60=80\text{ mm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

source.quote: A rectangular piece of paper is 4800mm 2

steps.content: Example: perimeter from area: A rectangle has area $28\text{ cm}^2$ and width $4\text{ cm}$. Find its perimeter. $\text{Length}=28\div4=7\text{ cm}$. $P=2(L+W)$. $P=2(7+4)=2\times11=22\text{ cm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: A rectangle has area $28\text{ cm}^2$ and width $4\text{ cm}$. Find its perimeter. $\text{Length}=28\div4=7\text{ cm}$. $P=2(L+W)$. $P=2(7+4)=2\times11=22\text{ cm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

source.quote: Find the perimeter of the rectangle whose area is 28cm 2

steps.content: A rectangle has area 45 square decimetres and width 5 dm. Find its perimeter. A rectangle has area 20 square centimetres and length 5 cm. Find its width. The perimeter of a rectangle is 18 cm and its length is 5 cm. Find its width. A rectangle has area 28 square centimetres and width 4 cm. Find its perimeter. Calculate the area of a rectangle whose length is 14 dm and width is 9 dm.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets these questions: A rectangle has area 45 square decimetres and width 5 dm. Find its perimeter. A rectangle has area 20 square centimetres and length 5 cm. Find its width. The perimeter of a rectangle is 18 cm and its length is 5 cm. Find its width. A rectangle has area 28 square centimetres and width 4 cm. Find its perimeter. Calculate the area of a rectangle whose length is 14 dm and width is 9 dm. The teacher checks each learner’s working, marks against these computed answers: Length = 45 ÷ 5 = 9 dm; P = 2(9 + 5) = 28 dm. 20 ÷ 5 = 4 cm. 18 ÷ 2 − 5 = 4 cm. Length = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 cm; perimeter = 2(7 + 4) = 22 cm. 14 × 9 = 126 dm². and supports learners who confuse lengths, areas or units.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners solve the questions individually, show each calculation, compare marked answers, and correct any errors in substitution or units.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to explain their solutions to these questions: A rectangle has area 45 square decimetres and width 5 dm. Find its perimeter. A rectangle has area 20 square centimetres and length 5 cm. Find its width. The perimeter of a rectangle is 18 cm and its length is 5 cm. Find its width. A rectangle has area 28 square centimetres and width 4 cm. Find its perimeter. Calculate the area of a rectangle whose length is 14 dm and width is 9 dm. The teacher checks the lesson objectives against the written work and assigns correction of the final exercise item.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their calculation methods, state the correct units, and correct the final exercise item after receiving feedback.
